item.title: TheHive/Cortex - v4.2.2 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\# Release Notes - v4.2.2: "The Pollen Sieve" 🌼 \## Summary Version 4.2.2 is a \*\*bug-fix release\*\* about things that used to fall through without a sound. A custom field of type \`url\` was dropped from every alert and case with no error at all; an empty "Job SID" let the create action fail deep inside the add-on instead of stopping at the form. Both are fixed, and the add-on now \*\*says something\*\* when it drops a custom field instead of staying silent. Splunk Cloud administrators (\`sc\_admin\`) also regain write access to the views and navigation. No new feature is introduced and no configuration change is required — this is a safe, drop-in update from v4.2.1. \## Improvements & Bug Fixes \### 🧩 Alert Actions: \`url\` custom fields are no longer dropped (\[#133]\(https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/issues/133)) \- \*\*Root cause\*\*: custom field values are only forwarded when their type is recognised by a chain handling \`string\`, \`boolean\`, \`integer\`, \`float\` and \`date\`. The \`url\` type, available since TheHive 5.1, was missing from that chain, so the field was skipped. The alert or case was still created, minus the field, and \*\*nothing was logged\*\* — the value simply never arrived. \- \*\*Fix\*\*: \`url\` carries a plain string value and is now handled exactly like \`string\`. Both "Create a new alert" and "Create a new case" are affected, as they share the same parsing routine. \- \*\*No more silence\*\*: a custom field dropped because its type is unmapped, or because its value does not match its declared type, is now logged as a warning (\`THC-117\`) naming both the field and the type. A future unknown type will be visible in the logs instead of costing a day of troubleshooting. \- \*\*Regression tests\*\*: the parsing routine gains its first unit tests. Every TheHive custom field type is now asserted to survive, and the "dropped but logged" behaviour is asserted too. \### 🖥️ Dashboards: the Job SID is now required (\[#132]\(https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/issues/132)) \- \*\*Root cause\*\*: "Job SID (input data)" was optional in the \*Create a new case\* and \*Create a new alert\* panels. Leaving it empty produced an empty \`| loadjob\`, and the failure surfaced far from its cause — a \`FileNotFoundError\` followed by \`UnboundLocalError: local variable 'rf' referenced before assignment\`, deep inside the alert action base. \- \*\*Fix\*\*: Splunk Simple XML has no \`required\` attribute, so the field now drives a token and the action panel depends on it. The action cannot run until a SID is entered, and the label carries a \`\*\` like the other mandatory fields. \### ☁️ Splunk Cloud: \`sc\_admin\` can write views and navigation \- \`metadata/default.meta\` granted write access on \`\[views]\` and \`\[nav]\` to the \`admin\` role only. Splunk Cloud customers hold \*\*\`sc\_admin\`\*\*, not \`admin\`, so those knowledge objects were unreachable for them. Both roles are now granted, matching what the app-level stanza already did. \### 📚 Documentation (\[#128]\(https://github.com/LetMeR00t/TA-thehive-cortex/issues/128)) \- The UC2 walkthrough screenshots predate the v4.0.0 UCC rework: they still show \*TheHive instance ID\* as free text and \*Alert mode\* as radio buttons, where both are now dropdowns named \*\*Instance\*\* and \*\*Alert mode\*\*. \- The screenshots could not be regenerated for this release, so the section now carries the \*\*field values in writing\*\*, read off the images themselves, including the fact that \`Severity\`, \`TLP\`, \`PAP\` and \`Scope\` are dropdowns rather than field names, and that \`Description\` expects the \*\*name of the field\*\* holding the text (\`info\` in the UC2 search). \## Under the hood These change nothing for users, but matter to anyone building the add-on: \- \*\*\`splunktaucclib\` 8.1.0 → 8.2.0\*\*, the minimum accepted by \`ucc-gen\` 6.5.3. Building with an older pin fails before any code is compiled. \- \*\*\`package/lib/requirements.txt\` is now versioned.\*\* It was silently excluded by the generic \`lib/\` rule of the Python \`.gitignore\`, which meant a fresh clone could not rebuild the same add-on. \- \*\*The test suite is now part of the repository.\*\* The unit tests mock every Splunk and network module and run anywhere; the integration tests read their endpoints and credentials from a local \`.env\`, which stays out of the repository. \- \`CONTRIBUTE.md\` gains the \*\*AppInspect step\*\*, which the build/package/deploy lifecycle did not describe. \## Splunk Cloud vetting Measured with AppInspect \*\*4.3.0\*\* (\`--mode precert --included-tags cloud\`) on the packaged \`.spl\`: \| | | \| :--- | :--- | \| \`error\` / \`failure\` | \*\*0 / 0\*\* | \| \`future\_failure\` | 1 | \| \`warning\` | 15 (all informational) | \| \`success\` | 136 | The remaining \`future\_failure\` is \`check\_for\_custom\_mako\_templates\`, on \`appserver/templates/base.html\`. \*\*It cannot be fixed from this repository\*\*: the file does not exist in the sources — \`ucc-gen\` generates it, the latest release (6.5.3) still does, and three generated views reference it (\`configuration.xml\`, \`dashboard.xml\`, \`inputs.xml\`). AppInspect advises regenerating with UCC ≥ 6.3.0, which does not remove it. It becomes blocking with Splunk Enterprise 10.4; the fix has to come from a future UCC release. \## Deployment Notes \- \*\*Prerequisite\*\*: Python 3.9 (matches Splunk's bundled interpreter). \- \*\*Migration Path\*\*: \- \*\*From v4.2.1 / v4.2.0 / v4.1.0 / v4.0.0\*\*: non-breaking update. Existing configuration, accounts, instances and certificates are preserved. \- \*\*From v3.9.0 (Direct Upgrade)\*\*: you can upgrade directly to v4.2.2. \- \*\*⚠️ CRITICAL\*\*: if upgrading from v3.x, the \*\*\[v4.0.0 migration instructions]\(./v4.0.0.md) are mandatory\*\* and remain valid for this version (UCC architecture migration, breaking configuration changes, and new credential storage). Please read them carefully before proceeding. \- \*\*After upgrading\*\*: if you use a custom field of type \`url\` in an alert action, it will start arriving in TheHive — check that the receiving custom field is the one you expect. \- \*\*Upgrade tip (Windows / on-prem)\*\*: never delete the app's \`local/\` folder. Stop Splunk, back up \`local/\`, deploy the new build, restore \`local/\`, then start Splunk.

item.title: WithSecure Elements Add-on - v1.0.7 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**Bug fix release** — reported by an external reviewer. **Recommended upgrade for anyone running v1.0.6 or earlier**, especially environments with dual-stack hosts or multi-homed machines. ### The bug The WithSecure Elements API returns `details.hostIpAddress` as a single JSON string that concatenates every IP the host is bound to, separated by spaces: ``` "hostIpAddress": "192.168.110.128/24 192.168.171.128/24 10.0.0.5/8" ``` Splunk's `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS = json` stored this as one flat string, so a search like: ``` index=main sourcetype="withsecure:epp:security_event" "details.hostIpAddress"="192.168.171.128/24" ``` never matched events where that address was not the first one in the string. In the reporter's test corpus 13/53 events had two IPs and were affected — the same pattern is present on any host with multiple network interfaces or a dual-stack (IPv4 + link-local) configuration. ### The fix A single search-time `EVAL` calculated field on the `security_event` sourcetype that splits the string into a real multivalue field: ``` [withsecure:epp:security_event] EVAL-details.hostIpAddress = split('details.hostIpAddress', " ") ``` **Search-time only:** * no impact on ingestion, no re-indexing needed * applies retroactively to events already in the index * 100 % reversible (remove the line to go back to a flat string) After upgrading, the following now behave consistently on every IP the host reports: * exact-match: `details.hostIpAddress="192.168.171.128/24"` * `IN()`: `details.hostIpAddress IN ("10.0.0.5/8", "192.168.171.128/24")` * `| mvexpand details.hostIpAddress` — one row per IP * `mvcount(details.hostIpAddress)` — actual count of IPs * CIM `src_ip` alias — respects the multivalue ### Upgrade safety Non-destructive in-place upgrade. KV Store checkpoints, input configuration, and existing indexed events are preserved.

Description:
The WithSecure Elements Add-on collects endpoint protection and detection data from the WithSecure Elements API. It ingests EPP Security Events and EDR Broad Context Detections through OAuth2-authenticated modular inputs, enabling centralized security event analysis in Splunk. The add-on maps collected events to CIM endpoint, malware, intrusion detection, and process tags, facilitating correlation with other security data sources. Two modular inputs handle data collection: withsecure_epp_input retrieves endpoint protection events, while withsecure_bcd_input collects EDR broad context detection incidents. Events are indexed under source types withsecure:epp:security_event, withsecure:epp:bcd_incident, and withsecure:epp:bcd_detection. The add-on includes a custom search command for retrieving specific detection details and provides a workflow action to fetch incident detections directly from the Splunk interface.
